problems.problem name: Preorder Traversal of a Binary Tree
problems.description: Implement a function to perform preorder traversal on a binary tree. In preorder traversal, visit nodes in this order: first visit the root node, then recursively traverse the left subtree, and finally recursively traverse the right subtree. For a tree with root 1, left child 2 (with children 4 and 5), and right child 3 (with children 6 and 7), the preorder traversal produces [1,2,4,5,3,6,7]. Only JavaScript is allowed.
problems.inputs description: Input is a binary tree represented as a nested dictionary. Each node has a value 'val' and pointers to its left and right children.
problems.expected description: An array representing the preorder traversal of the tree.

problems.problem name: Inorder Traversal of a Binary Tree
problems.description: Implement a function to perform inorder traversal on a binary tree. In inorder traversal, visit nodes in this order: first recursively traverse the left subtree, then visit the root node, and finally recursively traverse the right subtree. This traversal produces sorted order for binary search trees. For a tree with root 1, left child 2 (with children 4 and 5), and right child 3 (with children 6 and 7), the inorder traversal produces [4,2,5,1,6,3,7]. Only JavaScript is allowed.
problems.inputs description: Input is a binary tree represented as a nested dictionary. Each node has a value 'val' and pointers to its left and right children.
problems.expected description: An array representing the inorder traversal of the tree.

problems.problem name: Postorder Traversal of a Binary Tree
problems.description: Implement a function to perform postorder traversal on a binary tree. In postorder traversal, visit nodes in this order: first recursively traverse the left subtree, then recursively traverse the right subtree, and finally visit the root node. This traversal is useful for deleting trees or evaluating postfix expressions. For a tree with root 1, left child 2 (with children 4 and 5), and right child 3 (with children 6 and 7), the postorder traversal produces [4,5,2,6,7,3,1]. Only JavaScript is allowed.
problems.inputs description: Input is a binary tree represented as a nested dictionary. Each node has a value 'val' and pointers to its left and right children.
problems.expected description: An array representing the postorder traversal of the tree.
